clue.text: Odder moves restricting sentimentality shown by reformer

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hem in the sentimental word, holding it inside
the letters of odder move about into a new order

parts.note: goo is mawkish sentiment

explanation.surface: A reformer's strange gestures come over as sentimental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges the five letters into DODER, which 'restricting' then splits around the sentimental word.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-meaning but interfering campaigner for improvement is called by this hyphenated name.

clue.text: Say too much, upsetting Italian ruler

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the pieces upside down, reading them bottom to top

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means in 'say, a cat'
OD is an overdose, taking too much

explanation.surface: Someone talks too much and offends an Italian ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa was the head of state, a historic Italian ruler.

clue.text: Spouse to be homesick for America?

parts.note: to miss a place is to long for it when away
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A wife stuck abroad pines for America.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for one's wife, a spouse.

clue.text: Long look suppressed by British singleton

indicators.note: the British letters press down around the others, holding them inside

parts.note: to ache for something is to long for it
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: A single British person stifles a lingering gaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is an unattached person; an unmarried man is the example here.

clue.text: Be surprised about acceptable work at a pointless task

indicators.note: the word for being surprised goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to boggle is to be astonished
on, as in 'that's not on', means acceptable
to do a job is to work at it

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed that work on a pointless task is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work at' supplies DO, as in doing a job; the inserted pair lands after the second letter of the surprised word.
explanation.definitionFit: A boondoggle is wasteful, futile work that gives the appearance of being useful.

clue.text: Tradesman to go after gold

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A tradesman sets off in pursuit of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker of suits is a classic example of a craftsman or tradesman.

clue.text: Modern technology source including book linked to rejected science

indicators.note: the source word takes the book letter inside it

parts.note: a root is a source or origin

indicators.note: rejected sends the science letters back the other way

explanation.surface: A modern technological resource includes a book tied to discredited science.
explanation.definitionFit: The design and building of automated machines is a modern branch of engineering.

clue.text: Workers assigned to a Hebridean location

parts.note: staff are the workers of an organisation

explanation.surface: Workers are posted to a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: An uninhabited island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, home of Fingal's Cave.

clue.text: Artist breaking an agreement is an obsessive type

indicators.note: the artist letters break into the gap between the other pieces

parts.note: OK signals agreement
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist who breaks a deal is a fanatic.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a geeky enthusiast obsessed with a niche hobby, from the waterproof coats trainspotters wear.

clue.text: I'm ready to receive book

definitions.meaning: split as two words, '...' is what a catcher calls when ready for the ball

explanation.surface: Someone says they are ready to be handed a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a big scholarly volume, a weighty kind of book.

clue.text: Shabby to accept matter with contempt

indicators.note: the shabby word accepts the matter word inside it

parts.note: scaly is British slang for shabby or mean
a thing is a matter, as in 'the thing is'

explanation.surface: It is shabby to accept something with disdain.
explanation.walkthrough: SCALY in this informal sense means shabby or stingy, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking cuttingly and harshly, with scorn, is doing so with contempt.

clue.text: Team recalled accepting court orders

indicators.note: the reversed team word takes the court letters inside
recalled calls the team word back, reading it in reverse

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: A team is called back to accept court orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' gives EDIS, and 'accepting' places the court abbreviation before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrees issued by an authority are formal orders.

clue.text: Shady negotiator showing diplomacy when beset by swindler

indicators.note: the swindler surrounds the diplomacy word on both sides

parts.note: a conman is a swindler
tact is diplomacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: A dodgy go-between shows tact when surrounded by a fraudster.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermediary who makes connections, often in murky or underworld dealings, is a shady negotiator.

clue.text: A large study into small creatures has you working with birds

indicators.note: the first pieces go into the word for small creatures

parts.note: fry are young fish
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A big study of tiny animals has you handling birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport of training hawks to hunt is working with birds of prey.

clue.text: Reputation in theatre now negligible

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words theatre now negligible

explanation.surface: A reputation in the theatre now counts for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame and wide acclaim make up a person's reputation.

clue.text: Holiday with two women about to score? Gosh!

indicators.note: the pair of women letters go about the scoring word
two asks for the women letter twice

parts.note: to hit a target is to score
eek is an exclamation of alarm or surprise

explanation.surface: Someone on holiday with two women is about to score, to their own astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitsun week follows Whit Sunday, Pentecost, a traditional British holiday period.
explanation.definitionFit: The week beginning on Whit Sunday was once a common holiday week in Britain.

clue.text: Opening of fridge unlikely to change, producing cold

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: something rigid is inflexible

explanation.surface: Opening the fridge, which seldom changes, lets out cold air.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid means very cold, freezing.

clue.text: Object of worship picked up mother with movement claiming certainty

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up lifts the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: a god is worshipped
ma is mother
a tic is an involuntary movement

explanation.surface: Mum, with a twitch, raises the idol and claims she is sure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reads like a homophone signal, but here it reverses GOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dogmatic means asserting opinions as if they were certainly true.

clue.text: Pithy and good reason to abandon stand-up session?

parts.note: a comedy set is called off with no mic, no microphone to speak into

explanation.surface: A comic's reason for ditching the gig is short and sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnomic sayings are terse maxims, brief and full of meaning, so pithy.

clue.text: Break in voltage delivered by a charged body

parts.note: V is the symbol for voltage
a cation is a positively charged ion

explanation.surface: A power cut is caused by a charged particle.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday is a break from work or study.

clue.text: Article with appreciative comment about hot newsreader

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the exclamation goes about the hot letter

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of admiration
H stands for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A tabloid piece with an admiring remark about a sexy presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: The main presenter of a news broadcast is called by this title, a newsreader.

clue.text: Articles dismissed by certain homosexual churchmen

indicators.note: the article letters are sent out of the words that follow

parts.note: clear means certain, sure
gay means homosexual
a is the indefinite article; two of them make AA

explanation.surface: Gay churchmen are dismissed from posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed by' takes one A out of CLEAR and one out of GAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy is the collective term for priests and ministers, churchmen as a body.

clue.text: Pessimists clearly losing heart over cuts announced on the radio

indicators.note: a word losing its heart keeps only its outside letters
a radio broadcast is heard, so these words signal a sound-alike

parts.note: nicks are small cuts

explanation.surface: Doom-mongers lose heart over spending cuts reported on air.
explanation.definitionFit: People who distrust others' motives and expect the worst are a close match for pessimists.

clue.text: Represented now as McT so may be this?

definitions.text: Represented now as McT so may be this?

indicators.note: re-presented means set out again, with the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle over who a person named Mc-something might be.
explanation.walkthrough: A surname beginning McT is typically Scottish, so the bearer may be a woman from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a woman with a Mc surname, likely from Scotland.

clue.text: Encouragement to leave college during part of weekend

indicators.note: the college letter falls during the weekend day

parts.note: Sat, Saturday, is part of the weekend

explanation.surface: Leaving college at the weekend is encouraged.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting 'go away!' is urging someone to leave quickly.

clue.text: Money lost in strike location

indicators.note: the money letter is lost from inside the strike word

parts.note: to smite is to strike

explanation.surface: Money is lost during an industrial strike at a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place where something is situated, a location.

clue.text: Military leader occupying previous place

indicators.note: the officer occupies the space inside the previous word

parts.note: late means former or previous
OC is an officer commanding

explanation.surface: A commander occupies a former position.
explanation.definitionFit: To find or position something is to place it, as a verb.

clue.text: Military leader runs into crashed taxi — here's sign of wound

parts.note: CIC is a commander-in-chief

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the rearranged taxi
a crashed taxi is wrecked, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A general races into a wrecked cab and shows a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' makes ATIX, and 'into' sets the runs letter in its middle; CIC is a standard abbreviation for commander-in-chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicatrix is a scar, the mark left after a wound heals.
